Byte-diff source-store vs deployed copies of all 10 modified scripts/docs

self_demonstration.outcome_1_fresh_deploy_permits_transitio: CONFIRMED: bash .claude/scripts/update-task-status.sh --dry-run postflight 83 implement <session> printed '[deploy-check] Task 83: touched extension(s) verified fresh -- proceeding.' and previewed the completed transition, exit 0.
self_demonstration.outcome_2_stale_scratch_extension_refuse: CONFIRMED: same deployed script against a scratch fixture with a deliberately stale scratch extension printed the refusal message and exited 6, with state.json status and the plan file both unchanged (before == after).

observations: The post-deploy verify-deploy.sh --findings diff shows this task's OWN core-extension findings (5 script-drift entries) fully resolved, 0 new core findings. However, because deploy-headless.sh resyncs the WHOLE tree (all loaded extensions, not just core), this run also picked up a concurrent sibling session's in-flight literature-extension work (a new script literature-fidelity-audit.sh, a grown literature-index.md, and a task-77 state.json field 'blockers' not yet in the gate10 schema). These three new findings are unrelated to any file in this task's 12-entry file_scope and are not caused by this task's own edits -- they are a structural side effect of running a whole-tree deploy while a sibling session is mid-edit in a different extension, a known category of hazard batch-orchestration-guardrails.md already documents for concurrent deploys. Recorded here per the observation duty; not fixed by this task (out of scope).
